cover.tagline: One spell in, five spells out — a goblin horde that casts itself.
cover.identity: Zada, Hedron Grinder turns every cheap spell that targets only her into a copy for each other creature you control — so a one-mana cantrip aimed at your commander becomes a fistful of cards when the Goblins are out in force. You flood the board with token makers, fuel monster turns with rituals like Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual, and convert the frenzy into damage through Impact Tremors, storm payoffs like Grapeshot and Empty the Warrens, and sacrifice engines like Goblin Bombardment. It plays like a tribal aggro deck that suddenly combusts into a storm deck.

how_it_wins:
The table counts your 1/1s, files you under aggro-that-runs-out-of-gas, and points its removal somewhere else. Take the gift. Every body you land is a card Zada, Hedron Grinder cashes later: an instant or sorcery targeting only her is copied once for each other creature you control, so one red mana across four Goblins is five cards and a hasted team (stack 001). Build the board first. Hold the cantrip second.

She is not the deck, and most pilots get that backwards. Of the five verified lines here only two put her on the battlefield: 002 runs off Impact Tremors, 005 off Storm-Kiln Artist, and 004 states outright that she is in the command zone while the turn happens. One of the three engine targets wants her; the other two do not. So when she eats a removal spell, do not rebuy her and do not pass the turn sulking. Keep casting.

Your ramp is the swarm, not your lands. Battle Hymn adds {R} for each creature you control, Brightstone Ritual adds {R} for each Goblin on the battlefield, and Skirk Prospector turns any spare token into red at instant speed. The goldfish has you at 5.182 mana on turn six — an ordinary curve. On the big turn, count Goblins, not Mountains.

Pick your exit before you cast the first spell; you have three and they are not interchangeable. Impact Tremors turns eight storm tokens into 8 damage to each opponent with no attack step (stack 002). Fists of Flame turns the same board into trample and takes a seat off 30 in one swing (stack 003). Haze of Rage with Storm-Kiln Artist simply does not stop (stack 005) — and it hits nobody by itself, so it is fuel, not a kill. A storm payoff and a ritual arrive together in 26.5% of games at a mean turn of 4.91, so when that hand shows up, know which of the first two ends the game before you tap anything.

combo_lines.001: The clause the whole deck stands on runs four words: a copy of a spell isn't cast (CR 707.10). Zada's ability triggers on casting, so her own copies can never trigger her again, and they add nothing to any storm count. What they do is resolve — separately, in full, one per body, the haste and the draw alike. The holding: one red mana and one card buys five cards and a team that can attack. Every single-target cantrip in this list runs on that same clause.
combo_lines.002: Storm reads copy it for each other spell that was cast before it this turn (CR 702.40a), and the case turns on one word: cast. Storm's own copies are put onto the stack and never cast, so they raise nobody's count — not their own spell's, and not the Grapeshot you fire later in the same turn. Below, four resolutions buy eight tokens and eight damage to each opponent. Four casts is what the count is worth: a following Grapeshot is the fifth spell cast this turn and sees a storm count of 4. Those are different numbers, and the holding is to count your casts, not your resolutions.
combo_lines.003: Fists of Flame draws first and buffs second, and CR 608.2h decides what that ordering is worth: if an effect requires information from the game, the answer is determined only once, when the effect is applied. Each copy therefore prices its own +1/+0-per-card at its own resolution and never revises it. The buffs land ascending and they are final; nothing grows retroactively. One caution the record insists on, because this math comes out exactly lethal — a player at 0 or less life loses as a state-based action (CR 704.5a), checked after combat damage is dealt, not during.
combo_lines.004: Commander Spellbook files Krenko, Mob Boss with Skirk Prospector and Goblin Warchief as an infinite. The claim rests on CR 903.9a, which lets an owner move a commander out of a graveyard — and the rule says a commander. Yours is Zada. A Krenko put into the graveyard is a card in a graveyard and stays one. The battlefield route closes just as firmly: his ability costs {T}, only untapped permanents can be tapped (CR 701.26a), and nothing in this list untaps him. The holding: one cast, one activation, storm count one. What the record does affirm is set out below, and it is still a very good turn.
combo_lines.005: Buyback puts the spell into its owner's hand instead of the graveyard as it resolves (CR 702.27a) — the card, and only the card. The copies never see a hand at all: a copy of a spell in any zone other than the stack ceases to exist (CR 704.5e). That asymmetry is the engine, because every copy still fired magecraft on its way out. Affirmed: iteration k costs four mana and yields k+3 Treasures, mana-positive and strictly improving each time, unbounded. Where the record is silent is the kill — the loop touches no opponent and grants your team neither haste nor evasion.

card_roles.Zada, Hedron Grinder: Any instant or sorcery aimed at only her is copied once per other creature you control, which is the best rate in the deck and the only one the table lets you have for free. Cast your cantrip on the turn you have bodies, not the turn you draw it.
card_roles.Crimson Wisps: One mana, one target, one card — and across four bodies it is five cards plus a hasted team (stack 001). Hold it until the board is wide; it costs exactly the same either way.
card_roles.Expedite: The same one-mana blueprint: haste plus a card. Point it at Zada and everything you made this turn attacks this turn.
card_roles.Renegade Tactics: A one-mana cantrip that also says can't block. Copied across the board it strips the table's blockers and refills your hand at once — fire it precombat, every time.
card_roles.Witch's Mark: Discard a dead card, draw two, and staple a Wicked Role onto a creature. Use it to convert the ritual you cannot cast yet into two live cards.
card_roles.Fists of Flame: Your combat finisher: each copy draws, then locks in +1/+0 per card drawn this turn, and everything gains trample (stack 003). Do the arithmetic before you cast — the buffs land ascending and a single blocker eats almost nothing through trample.
card_roles.Ancestors' Aid: +2/+0, first strike and a Treasure off one target. Copied, that is a team anthem plus a Treasure per body, so cast it before the expensive spell and spend what it makes.
card_roles.Wild Ride: +3/+0 and haste for one mana on one target, which becomes a board-wide anthem through the copy hub. It harmonizes back from the graveyard for {4}{R} — less if you tap a creature — so pitching it early costs you nothing.
card_roles.Frontline Heroism: A copy hub that needs no legend: every spell targeting only one of your creatures makes a hasty Soldier and then copies that spell at the new token. Deploy it before the pivot turn, never during it.
card_roles.Dragon Fodder: Two bodies for two mana, which is two more copies off every cantrip and two more damage triggers. Turn-two play, not a storm-turn play.
card_roles.Krenko's Command: The identical two-for-two. Run these out early — the copies they enable later are worth far more than the one cast they add to a storm count.
card_roles.Empty the Warrens: The storm payoff (stack 002). Cast three cheap spells first: that is the entire difference between four tokens and eight, and under Impact Tremors it is the difference between 4 and 8 damage to every opponent.
card_roles.Haze of Rage: Buyback {2} plus storm plus a team pump, and with Storm-Kiln Artist out it stops being a spell and becomes a loop that pays for itself (stack 005). Line up your damage outlet before you start it — the loop alone kills nobody.
card_roles.Spreading Insurrection: Storm on a threaten effect: each copy steals another untapped creature, hasted, until end of turn. Cast it late in the chain and swing with the table's own board, then feed the borrowed bodies to a sacrifice outlet before you give them back.
card_roles.Grapeshot: One damage per instance at your storm count, aimed anywhere. It is your reach for the last few points and your answer to a critical x/1 — remember your own copies never raise the count.
card_roles.Impact Tremors: One damage to each opponent per creature entering, which turns a token spell into a table-wide burn spell. Land it before the storm turn, not after; it is the difference between eight tokens and 8 to every seat.
card_roles.General Kreat, the Boltbringer: A free attacking token whenever your Goblins attack, and 1 to each opponent whenever another creature of yours enters. On the storm turn he is a second Impact Tremors — count him in your damage math before you fire.
card_roles.Boggart Shenanigans: Every other Goblin of yours that dies pings a player for 1. With a free sacrifice outlet out, a board that is about to be swept is damage on the way out — spend it rather than mourning it.
card_roles.Goblin Bombardment: A free, repeatable sacrifice outlet that deals damage at instant speed. Sacrifice in response to exile or bounce and aim at faces; this is how a swarm still converts after it stops being allowed to attack.
card_roles.Pashalik Mons: Every Goblin death of yours is 1 damage anywhere, and {3}{R} plus a Goblin buys two more. Point the pings at players when nothing needs killing.
card_roles.Skirk Prospector: Free sacrifice outlet and your fastest ritual: any Goblin becomes {R} with nothing on the stack for the table to respond to. Never feed him Krenko.
card_roles.Broadside Bombardiers: Menace and haste, and after it attacks you may sacrifice another creature or artifact to deal 2 plus that permanent's mana value to any target. Boast once per turn, so attack first and pick the target after blocks.
card_roles.Siege-Gang Commander: Three tokens on arrival and a repeatable {1}{R}, sacrifice a Goblin, 2 damage. That second mode is your reach when the ground gums up — spend leftover tokens at faces.
card_roles.Siege-Gang Lieutenant: Two hasty tokens at the beginning of each of your combats while you control your commander. That is a second reason to keep Zada alive that has nothing to do with copying spells.
card_roles.Mogg War Marshal: Two bodies now and one more when it dies, for two mana. Let the echo lapse on purpose when you have a sacrifice outlet — the death token is part of the deal.
card_roles.Searslicer Goblin: A free token at every end step in which you attacked. Attack with something, even a lone 1/1 you can afford to lose.
card_roles.Howlsquad Heavy: Haste for your other Goblins and a free attacking token every combat, with a max-speed tap for {R} per Goblin behind it. Treat the haste as the reason he is here and the mana as the bonus.
card_roles.Impulsive Pilferer: A one-mana Goblin that leaves a Treasure when it dies, so sacrificing it turns a body into mana. Encore it for {3}{R} from the graveyard when the board is empty.
card_roles.Redcap Gutter-Dweller: Menace, two Rat tokens on entry, and an upkeep sacrifice that grows it and exiles you a card to play. Feed it the token you were sacrificing anyway.
card_roles.Goblin Bushwhacker: Kick it for the extra {R} and the whole team gets +1/+0 and haste. That is your out-of-nowhere alpha strike; unkicked it is a 1/1 that adds one to your cast count.
card_roles.Goblin Chieftain: +1/+1 and haste for every other Goblin. Haste is the word that matters — tokens made this turn swing this turn.
card_roles.Goblin Warchief: Goblin spells cost {1} less and your Goblins have haste, which is exactly why Krenko costs {1}{R}{R} and activates the turn he lands (stack 004). Play him before the wave, not after it.
card_roles.Goblin Trashmaster: An anthem for the swarm plus a repeatable sacrifice-a-Goblin to destroy an artifact. Against a rocks-and-equipment table that is removal you get to use every turn.
card_roles.Rundvelt Hordemaster: +1/+1 to your other Goblins, and every Goblin death exiles the top card — Goblin creature cards are castable until the end of your next turn. With him out, sacrifice freely.
card_roles.Quest for the Goblin Lord: One mana, and once five Goblins have entered the whole team gets +2/+0. A single Empty the Warrens or one Krenko activation fills it in one go, so play it on turn one and let the swarm do the work.
card_roles.Krenko, Mob Boss: Doubles your Goblin count once, and only once — his ability taps, nothing here untaps him, and he is not your commander, so a Krenko in the graveyard stays there (stack 004). Play him for the burst and never sacrifice him.
card_roles.Goblin Lackey: Connect once and a Goblin permanent walks out of your hand for free. Send him at the open seat on turn two; a free Siege-Gang Commander is not a fantasy.
card_roles.Goblin Matron: Tutors any Goblin card straight to hand. Default to whichever engine piece is missing — Skirk Prospector for mana, Goblin Warchief for the discount, Krenko for bodies.
card_roles.Moggcatcher: {3} and a tap fetches a Goblin permanent onto the battlefield, skipping the cast entirely. Slow, so activate it on a turn you were not going to storm anyway, and take the piece you cannot afford to hard-cast.
card_roles.Conspicuous Snoop: Play with your top card revealed, cast Goblin spells off the top, and borrow the activated abilities of any Goblin sitting there. Check the top of your library before you plan a turn — it is a free card of information every single turn.
card_roles.Gempalm Incinerator: Cycle it for {1}{R} to draw and deal damage equal to your Goblin count. Know the trap: cycling is an ability, not a cast, so it adds nothing to your storm count — take the removal anyway.
card_roles.Goblin Dark-Dwellers: Menace, and on entry he casts an instant or sorcery of mana value 3 or less from your graveyard for free. Aim him at a spent ritual like Seething Song mid-storm-turn, not at a cantrip.
card_roles.Grenzo, Havoc Raiser: Every creature of yours that connects either goads something that would have blocked or exiles the top of that player's library for you to cast. Use goad to point the table's biggest body at the seat that is actually threatening you.
card_roles.Battle Hymn: Two mana at instant speed for {R} per creature you control — with a mean of 4.068 bodies by turn five, that is a profit the moment your third token lands. Cast it after the token spell, never before.
card_roles.Brightstone Ritual: One mana for {R} per Goblin on the battlefield, counting everyone's. On a swarm board it is the cheapest ritual in the deck; hold it for the turn you intend to go off.
card_roles.Seething Song: Three mana for five, no board required. This is the ritual that works from an empty battlefield — save it for a hand of payoffs and nothing to attack with.
card_roles.Mana Geyser: {R} for each tapped land your opponents control, so its size is somebody else's decision. Go off after the table has spent its turn, not before.
card_roles.Glimpse the Impossible: Exile three off the top and play them this turn; the leftovers become 0/1 Eldrazi Spawn that sacrifice for {C}. Cast it early in the chain so you have the mana to use what it finds.
card_roles.Great Train Heist: Spree, so pay for what the turn needs: {2}{R} untaps your team and adds a combat, {2} pumps and gives first strike, {R} makes Treasures off combat damage. Buy the extra combat when your board is already lethal-ish, not when you are digging.
card_roles.Storm-Kiln Artist: A Treasure for every instant or sorcery you cast or copy, which makes him the copy hub's paymaster and half of the loop (stack 005). Play him when the table's removal is spent — he is the piece they must kill.
card_roles.Past in Flames: Every instant and sorcery in your graveyard gains flashback for the turn, which after a spent ritual chain is a second storm turn out of nowhere. Cast it at the bottom of the chain, once the graveyard is stocked.
card_roles.Faithless Looting: Two cards deep for one mana, and flashback {2}{R} means the card comes back. Loot away the rituals you cannot fund and the payoffs you cannot pay for.
card_roles.Daring Discovery: Three creatures can't block, then discover 4 casts you a free spell of mana value 4 or less. Cast it precombat when the swing is close, not as a card-draw spell.
card_roles.Idol of Oblivion: Tap to draw a card in any turn you made a token, which in this deck is most of them. Play it early — it is only good on the turns you were going to have anyway.
card_roles.Skullclamp: Equip {1} onto a 1/1 and it dies for two cards. This is why a sweeper is a draw step rather than a loss; keep one mana up when the table is threatening one.
card_roles.Swiftfoot Boots: Hexproof and haste, equip {1}. Suit up Zada on the turn you intend to cast a payload, not the turn she lands — protection you paid for a turn early is protection you gave away.
card_roles.Roaming Throne: Ward {2}, and triggered abilities of your other creatures of the chosen type trigger an extra time. Name Goblin and every attack trigger, death trigger and enters-trigger on your board fires twice.
card_roles.Ruby Medallion: Red spells cost {1} less, which on a two-mana average is roughly a free spell for every two you cast. It is a storm-turn multiplier disguised as a rock — play it on the quiet turns.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Two colourless on turn one is a whole extra turn of development. Nothing in this deck would rather have anything else on the play.
card_roles.Throne of Eldraine: Four red at once, but only to cast monocoloured red spells — it cannot pay an equip, an activation or a sacrifice cost anywhere in this deck. Cast the spells with it and pay for everything else another way.
card_roles.Blasphemous Act: Thirteen damage to each creature, costing {1} less per creature on the battlefield, so against a wide table it is nearly free. It kills your own swarm too — cast it from behind, with Skullclamp equipped or a sacrifice outlet open.
card_roles.Chaos Warp: Your only answer to the classes nothing else here touches: an enchantment, a planeswalker, a resolved anything. Save it for the permanent that actually beats you, not the biggest one.
card_roles.Vandalblast: One mana kills one artifact you do not control; overload {4}{R} kills all of them and never touches yours. Against a rock-heavy table the overload is a one-sided sweeper — wait for two targets minimum.
card_roles.Goblin Negotiation: X damage to a creature, and the excess damage comes back as 1/1 Goblins. Aim it at a small creature with a large X when you want the tokens more than the kill.
card_roles.Mountain: Twenty-two of them, which is why the colour maths in this issue is boring. Play one every turn and stop overthinking it.
card_roles.Arena of Glory: Taps for {R}, and for {R} and an exert it makes {R}{R} that grants haste to a creature spell. Exert it on the turn you cast a fat Goblin you need attacking immediately, and accept it staying tapped.
card_roles.Castle Embereth: Enters untapped once you control a Mountain, and {1}{R}{R} plus a tap pumps the whole team +1/+0. On a ten-token board that activation is ten damage — hold the mana in combat.
card_roles.Den of the Bugbear: A land that becomes a 3/2 Goblin for {3}{R} and makes a tapped attacking token every time it swings. Activate it on turns you have spare mana and no spell worth casting.
card_roles.Dwarven Mine: Enters untapped with three other Mountains out and gives you a 1/1 Dwarf when it does. Play your basics first so this one arrives on the profitable side.
card_roles.Goblin Burrows: Colourless for mana, but {1}{R} and a tap gives a Goblin +2/+0 — a repeatable damage sink for leftover mana in combat. Note it needs real mana, not Throne of Eldraine's.
card_roles.Kher Keep: {1}{R} and a tap makes a 0/1 Kobold, which is another body for the copy hub and another sacrifice for the outlets. Make one on any turn you would otherwise waste two mana.
card_roles.Shinka, the Bloodsoaked Keep: Taps for {R} and gives a legendary creature first strike for {R}. Small, but it wins a combat over Zada that would otherwise kill her.
card_roles.Spinerock Knoll: Hideaway 4 on entry, and the exiled card is free once an opponent has taken 7 or more damage in a turn. This deck deals 7 to a seat routinely — play it early so the hidden card is there when the storm turn lands.
card_roles.Hidden Volcano: Enters tapped, taps for {R}, and sacrifices at sorcery speed for {4}{R} to discover 4. That is a late-game mana sink; use it on a turn you have nothing else to spend on.
card_roles.Forgotten Cave: Enters tapped, or cycles for {R} when you have enough lands. Cycle it the moment your third land is on the table.
card_roles.Smoldering Crater: The same deal at cycling {2}. Land drop early, card later — decide by turn two which one this game needs.
card_roles.Fountainport: Colourless, and every mode matters here: {2} and a sacrificed token draws a card, {4} makes a Treasure, {3} and a life makes a body. Spend leftover tokens through it at the end of a turn you did not go off.
card_roles.Reliquary Tower: No maximum hand size, which matters on the turns the copy hub draws you five cards in one cast. It makes no red mana — count it out of your colour maths.
card_roles.War Room: {3}, a tap and 1 life draws a card in a mono-coloured deck, the cheapest rate the land offers anybody. Use it on the turns you have mana and no play.

mulligan:
Most players mulligan hunting for the payoff. You do not have to. Zada waits in the command zone at four mana and lands on a mean turn of 4.35, with 90% of games having her cast by turn six. Your opening seven does not need a win condition in it.

Keep three lands — or two plus Sol Ring, Skirk Prospector or Ruby Medallion — alongside a cheap token maker like Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command, Mogg War Marshal or Searslicer Goblin, and bank a one-mana cantrip for the turn Zada resolves. That is the ordinary hand here, not the dream: 79.1% of first sevens clear the keep rule and the average game costs you a quarter of a mulligan. Keep the ordinary hand.

Ship the hands that are all payoff and no setup. Mana Geyser, Empty the Warrens and Blasphemous Act on two lands is a mulligan every time — rituals need a board and storm needs a cast count. A storm payoff and a ritual arrive together in only 26.5% of games, so stop waiting for that seven and take the one that makes bodies on turn two. An early token maker is the thing that actually shows up: 60.0% of games, mean turn 3.18.

Two cards rescue a marginal keep. Faithless Looting and Witch's Mark both trade dead cards for live ones for two mana or less, so lands plus one body plus a looter is a keep — snap it off and dig.

One habit for the big turns: say your cast count out loud, and say it on the cast, not on the resolution. Copies go on the stack without being cast and they never raise the count (stack 002). Ten-spell turns are precisely where good pilots miscount and fire Grapeshot two short.
upgrades:
Seventy-six at one end, 13,958 at the other — a factor of 184. Deflecting Swat at 76 sits seventh on the list, Seething Anger at 13,958 sits tenth, and the median is about 1,060. Popularity is a column here, not the sort.

Nine of the ten cost three or less, five of them exactly three, for a mean of 2.5 against a deck whose modal mana value is 2. Six permanents, four spells. Five entries name the slot they would take; five name nothing.

Three of the ten point at an axis the audit calls a weakness, and only one moves a count. Soul-Guide Lantern takes measured interaction breadth from two answered permanent classes to three — graveyard is the class no card in the 99 touches. Deflecting Swat and Champion's Helm both land on protection, which reads 2: the densest overlap here.

Seven infinite-flagged lines across three cards — three on Reiterate, three on Thornbite Staff, one on Seething Anger — and zero of the seven are verified. Every entry carries a bracket delta of 4 to 4. The floor already sits at 4 off a single two-card infinite that assembles at mana value 4, and Jeska's Will, the only Game Changer any of these would add, does not move it.

The thinnest measured rate in the deck is 26.5% — storm payoff plus ritual, four payoff cards deep — against 66.1% for the Zada-and-a-cantrip target and 60.0% for early tokens. Not one of these ten is a payoff. Birgi, God of Storytelling and Jeska's Will buy the mana half; Reiterate and Seething Anger buy storm count. The list works around that 26.5% rather than into it.

One of the three targets is commander-gated, and the fastest — early tokens, 60.0% at a mean turn of 3.184 — is not. The protection pair leans the other way: Champion's Helm equips Zada, and Deflecting Swat's free cast needs her on the battlefield. Both are cheap. Worth knowing which half of the deck that budget buys.
mana_base:
Thirty-six land copies across fifteen entries, twenty-two of them Mountains. Eight enter tapped — 22% of the base, inside the usual one-in-three budget — and five of those eight do it no matter what you control. Pip share 1.00, source share 1.00. Mono-red leaves nothing to arbitrate.

Thirty-three of the thirty-six make red, against a target of 36 — a target asking every land in the deck to produce red. The three that do not are Reliquary Tower, War Room and Fountainport, in the list for what they do rather than what they tap for. Call that 36 a yardstick, not a possibility. Lands alone still put red on curve 86.9% of the time.

The demand side is light, which is why 86.9% reads comfortable. Sixty-nine red pips across 57 cards, first needed on turn one, and the heaviest ask anywhere is {R}{R} — effective pip requirement 2. A deck whose worst colour requirement is two red does not need that thirty-sixth source the way a triple-pip deck would.

Rocks and dorks lift the count to 43 sources and the on-curve figure to 96%, and that flatters what the ramp is: six rituals, four dorks, one rock, three cost-reducers. Rituals are not sources. They add mana to one turn, not per turn — the only unit a storm count trades in. Battle Hymn against a mean of 4.068 bodies on turn five is a two-mana instant that hands you about four red. Throne of Eldraine adds four, spells-only, so it cannot pay Skullclamp's equip or Goblin Burrows' pump, and it never appears in the 43.

Turn by turn it is ordinary. Land drops hit 90.0% on turn three, 63.7% on turn five and 38.2% by turn ten; mean available mana runs 3.937 on turn four, 4.589 on turn five and 6.964 on turn ten. Five mana has never stormed anybody out of a game. The base's job is delivering that five reliably — the rituals and the swarm are the multiplier on top.
threat_assessment:
Three opponents see a four-mana Goblin who copies cantrips and decide that killing her kills the deck. Let them keep that read. It is wrong.

Only stacks 001 and 003 need Zada on the battlefield: 002 kills off Impact Tremors, 005 loops off Storm-Kiln Artist, 004 has her in the command zone. Pilot her as a luxury, never as life support. Equip the Boots on the turn you draw five cards; let her eat removal otherwise.

Sequence to stay dull. Lead with bodies — 2.36 by turn three, your token maker by 3.18 — and let the table read chump blockers. Cast Zada on curve and do nothing; she lands turn four in 7,002 runs of 10,000, so hand them the 3/3 they circled and pass with red you will not spend. Play Impact Tremors onto one or two Goblins, where it pings for one and reads as durdle. Hold the loud cards — Storm-Kiln Artist, Krenko, Conspicuous Snoop — until removal has found other homes. Snoop shows your library top to every seat: cast him when you want the Goblin off the top, not when you draw him.

Read their mana before your hand. Two blue untapped is the counter, four white is the wrath: take value into open mana, fire the engine into a tapped-out table.

You pick the turn you become archenemy. There are three. Zada untapped, three bodies, one red — stack 001, five cards and a hasted team. Storm-Kiln Artist, four up, Haze of Rage — stack 005; that first buyback cast is your commitment point, so never make it into untapped blue. Impact Tremors or General Kreat with a ritual behind a payoff — stack 002 takes eight off every seat from 1/1s. Sequence the pingers before the payoff, always.

Their script is short: kill Storm-Kiln Artist in response to the first magecraft trigger, or answer the Treasures at instant speed. Make them run it with mana already spent.

Krenko, Mob Boss is your best misinformation. Stack 004 says the famous loop terminates here: he taps, nothing untaps him, and he is not your commander. Cast him for what he is — five tokens, thirteen power with haste. When a seat burns removal on a loop you do not have, take the trade quietly. Never spend protection on him; never feed him to Prospector expecting him back.

Count only what you can see: mana up, cards in hand, bodies on board. Build toward Zada with a payload — 66.1%, mean turn 5.27 — and take the ritual-and-payoff ceiling, 26.5% at 4.91, when it arrives.

Then wear the hat. The turn you draw five cards in front of three opponents, they answer you or start dying — and you chose the turn.
matchups:
Every seat's second plan is just "kill the commander." Take it away.

Against removal, let Zada die and keep casting. Impact Tremors, General Kreat, Storm-Kiln Artist and Frontline Heroism work with her in the command zone; Heroism copies your targeted spell at a hasty Soldier, no legend needed. Recast her only with a payload in hand: two mana and a turn not advancing.

Against sweeper control, your engine is wrath insurance: hand and Treasures sit where a sweeper cannot reach. Fire cantrips into the telegraphed wrath — stack 001 banks the draws for one red mana. Never hold back; time is their plan. Their one instant answer is a counter saved for your kill: make them spend it on a cantrip. Then charge rent: Skullclamp makes each dying 1/1 two cards for {1}, Pashalik Mons pings per dying Goblin, Goblin Bombardment converts the rest. Always hold a token maker.

Stax and tax attack your arithmetic. Recount your hand under the tax: a two-spell turn that becomes one halves the engine. Break the first piece early — Vandalblast overloads for {4}{R}, Goblin Trashmaster eats a Goblin to kill an artifact, Chaos Warp handles what nothing else touches. Aim at the piece beating you, not the one scaring you. Under mana denial keep casting: Ruby Medallion and Goblin Warchief pay the toll, Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual run off bodies. Land drops are 63.7% by turn five, 54.2% by six anyway: budget the big turn out of Goblins.

In mirrors and aggro pods, take the control seat: 4.07 bodies by turn five, 5.26 by six — block, trade, let 40 life carry you. Hold Blasphemous Act as your reset, not spot removal: {1} cheaper per creature out, and you alone rebuild. Count their Goblins before cycling Gempalm Incinerator. Win where blockers do not matter: Impact Tremors and General Kreat drain every seat with no attack. Let the other token deck wear the hat.

Against combo, spend interaction early. Thirteen copies over two of five permanent classes buy one cheap disruption at the decisive moment — rank seats by combo proximity, not board presence. Do not race: 26.5% at mean turn 4.91 is a ceiling, not a promise. Punish the setup turn; goad with Grenzo at the closest seat.

Refuse to play around graveyard hate. Past in Flames, Faithless Looting's flashback and Wild Ride's harmonize want a graveyard; under Rest in Peace, write the rebuild off and lean on token makers and Skullclamp.

Copies are not casts — stack 002's Grapeshot behind Empty the Warrens sees storm count 4.
editors_letter:
The deck on this cover is a Goblin deck the way a bonfire is a woodpile.

Zada, Hedron Grinder does exactly one thing. A spell that points at her and at nothing else is copied once for every other creature you control — so the Goblins are not a board, they are an exchange rate, and every cheap red spell in the ninety-nine is priced in them. The other half of the deck is a storm deck that never asked for her at all, and the two halves take turns being the game.

You will have a good time here if you enjoy arithmetic done fast and in public: counting casts, counting bodies, counting how much damage three separate seats are going to take, and living with the fact that getting one of those counts wrong ends your turn tapped out with everybody alive. You will not, if you want a board that frightens people. This is a pile of 1/1s until the turn it is not, and trying to look dangerous before then is how you lose the turn you were saving them for.

Two arguments in the log are worth the cover price. Coach Brightside opens by naming the two cards he thinks this deck is really bounded by, and Ledger has to tell him nobody has ever measured them. And there is a famous infinite combo inside these ninety-nine that is not infinite here — the Counselor has the reason, and it turns out she has two.

Read the log before you shuffle.

pilots_log.text: Exactly two cards in this deck deal damage to all three opponents when a creature shows up. Neither one is Zada. Everybody is watching the commander and everybody is counting the storm count, and the two cards that actually decide whether you kill three people or annoy them are cards you have never once mulliganed for: Impact Tremors and General Kreat, the Boltbringer. Those are the only two in the ninety-nine that turn a body entering into damage at EVERY seat. Two. Everything else you are proud of makes you pick somebody and split it up a point at a time.

The count is right, and then the record does something I have not had to say about a deck before.

Two cards. Impact Tremors reads that whenever a creature you control enters, it deals 1 damage to each opponent; General Kreat, the Boltbringer carries that same conversion attached to a body. Nothing else in the ninety-nine spreads it without you choosing a seat.

Now the part the Coach cannot have from me. Stack 002 is a checker-passed board and Impact Tremors is standing on it. But the citation that would let this magazine draw a solid line from the token flood to the damage is assembled from what a scenario names on the stack, in hand and in the graveyard, and it stops once it has two cards. Impact Tremors was on the battlefield, which that pass never reads. So the arrow prints dashed and I may not hand you the conversion as proven — on the single most famous turn this deck has.

The holding, plainly: the board resolved and I cannot certify the arrow. That is a hole in our paperwork rather than in the enchantment, and I would rather tell you than round it up.

There is no rate for the Coach's pair, and that is the whole finding.

Three targets have been declared for this deck and measured across ten thousand seeded runs. Zada plus a payload spell: assembled in 66.1% of runs, 49.6% by turn six, mean turn 5.27. An early token maker: 60.0%, 48.7% by turn six, mean turn 3.18. A storm payoff together with a ritual: 26.5%, 16.9% by turn six, mean turn 4.91.

An each-opponent damage payoff alongside a token maker is not one of them. The simulator has never been pointed at that pair. So I have a count and no rate — two cards in ninety-nine — while the three things that were measured price the hub's ammunition, an early body and the ceiling. The number Coach wants does not exist, and I am not going to invent it for him.

No number. Fine. I will take the count and play off the count.

So it changes two things you do. First, when you look at seven cards, ask whether they put a body on the table by turn three — the rest of this deck is multipliers, and a multiplier needs something to multiply. Second, when one of those two payoffs turns up, play it into an empty board on a boring turn and let them have it if they want it. You want it already down and already ignored before the flood, not held in hand for the big turn.

And when the big turn comes, count damage per seat before you tap out. Not total. Per seat. Three players on forty is a hundred and twenty life, and nobody has ever added their way through that.

Per seat, and per cast — because the count does not compound, and this is the technicality I would have tattooed on a Goblin.

Stack 002, on the record. Empty the Warrens cast as the fourth spell of the turn storm-triggers for three copies; four resolutions put eight tokens on the table. The next spell you cast that turn sees a storm count of four. Not seven. Rule 702.40a copies the spell for each other spell that was cast before it this turn, and 707.10 is the fence I enjoy most: 'a copy of a spell isn't cast.' Eight bodies arrived and the ledger of casts moved by exactly one.

In plain English: copies pay you in bodies and never in count. A spell whose size comes from how much you have cast wants to go late; a spell whose size comes from how many bodies you have wants to go after the tokens. Those are two different orders, and this deck will ask you for both inside the same turn.

Which turn, though. The storm payoff and the ritual arrive together in 26.5% of runs, 16.9% of them by turn six, mean turn 4.91 — and that pair is an AND of two independent draws, four payoff cards at 25.8% of opening sevens and four rituals at the same 25.8%.

The median game is the other thing entirely. Mean available mana at turn five is 4.589, by which point the land-drop hit rate has fallen to 63.7%. Bodies on board: 2.36 at turn three, 4.07 at turn five, 5.26 at turn six. The commander is cast at a mean turn of 4.35, median four, and 90.0% of runs have her by turn six.

Nine games in ten have the commander. One in four has the storm turn. Whatever you are practising, practise the first one.

Nine in ten. So play like she is coming, and play like she is leaving, because they will kill her — everybody kills her.

That is survivable, and here is why I do not panic about it. You are not one card deep on the copy effect. Frontline Heroism does the same job with no legend attached: point a cheap spell at one of your creatures, it builds you a Soldier and copies the spell at it. Rebuild, keep cantripping, make them find a second answer.

Coach. Read it again, slowly, because the deck's whole redundancy story is resting on that sentence.

Frontline Heroism creates one Soldier token and copies the spell once, at that token. Once. Not once per creature you control. Compare what the hub does: Zada's trigger copies the spell for each other creature it could target, and stack 001 has four Goblin tokens out and produces four copies plus the original — five cards off a single {R}. Read as printed, the enchantment makes one copy on a board of four and one copy on a board of ten. That is redundancy for the effect and not for the multiplier, and the gap between those two things is the engine.

I will also tell you what I do not have. No scenario in this deck has resolved Frontline Heroism, so what I just gave you is a reading of printed text and not a ruling — it sits among this deck's open questions, next to whether Roaming Throne's extra trigger reaches Zada's copy ability at all. And while we are auditing things written up as insurance: Roaming Throne's ward protects Roaming Throne.

Plainly: do not plan a turn around the Soldier as though it were a second commander. Nobody has proved it either way, and the text does not read kindly.

Taken, and it costs me a line I have been telling people.

So she is not replaceable — and she is also not required, which is the half people miss. When she dies the plan is not rebuild the hub. The plan is switch halves. Cast the cheap spells for what is printed on them, keep making Goblins, keep the rituals for a turn that pays, and pay her tax when the copy count is worth the four mana. Five cards for one red is worth it. Four mana to put a 3/3 in front of a removal spell is not.

The record backs the switch, as a count. Five stacks have passed the checker on this deck. Zada is on the battlefield in two of them, 001 and 003. She is absent from 002 and from 005, and 004 states outright that she is in the command zone. Of the fifteen lines drawn in this deck's engine, ten carry a passing stack and five do not.

One more count, and it points the other way. Protection is two copies against a target of five to seven, and the role table files both of them as protecting themselves. Two cards, and one of them is Swiftfoot Boots.

Two cards, and one of them is a pair of boots. Which brings me to the card the table actually reacts to.

You cast Krenko, Mob Boss and somebody says the word combo out loud, because everyone has seen Krenko and Skirk Prospector do the thing on the internet. Here is what I want you to know while they are pointing at you: in this deck it does not do the thing. Cast him anyway. Cast him when you already hold the payoff, take the bodies and the mana, and let them spend a removal spell on a Goblin that was never going to loop.

Correct, and there are two independent reasons, which is one more than I needed.

Stack 004 puts the board up and takes the claim apart. Krenko cast under Goblin Warchief locks at {1}{R}{R} and has haste, so he taps the turn he lands; his ability checks the count on resolution — five Goblins, counting himself — and makes five tokens, leaving ten Goblins on the table and up to ten one-shot red mana through Skirk Prospector if you are willing to empty the board to get it. All real, all measured.

The loop is not. The combo record's version needs Krenko recast over and over, which works only because rule 903.9a lets a COMMANDER be taken from the graveyard back to the command zone. Zada is the commander in this deck. Sacrifice Krenko here and he lies in the graveyard being a normal card. And even if you never sacrifice him: 701.26a, only untapped permanents can be tapped, and he is tapped, and nothing in these ninety-nine untaps him.

The holding: it is a spike, not a loop. One cast, one activation, and a phase's worth of mana that expires when the phase does.

Four combo lines sit fully inside this deck. Three of them are the Krenko lines the Counselor just took apart. The fourth is Storm-Kiln Artist with Haze of Rage, and it is the one with a passing stack behind it — 005, where cast one puts three copies and four Treasures down, cast two puts four and five, and the board finishes on nine Treasures against a four-Treasure price per iteration.

The rest of the shape, for the pilot: 79 entries, 15 of them lands at 36 copies, of which the artifact counts 33 as red sources — and that 33 includes a land whose only printed mana ability adds colourless, so read it as a ceiling. Curve: fifteen ones, nineteen twos, thirteen threes, ten fours, six fives, one nine. Keep-your-first-seven rate 79.1%, mean mulligans 0.255, and 3,003 opening sevens in ten thousand held exactly two lands.

Then here is your game, and it is shorter than this conversation.

Bodies by turn three. Put the each-seat payoff down early and boring, before anybody is frightened of you. Cast your count-scaling spell last and your body-scaling spell after the tokens. When the hub is gone, switch halves instead of grieving. When Krenko lands and the table says combo, smile and take the five bodies.

And on the turn you go: count the seats, out loud if you have to. This deck has never once lost because the pilot counted too carefully. It loses because somebody added up a hundred and twenty life, liked the total, and tapped out.
